threat: Producer intentionally ships harmful code
note: SLSA v1.2: not mitigated by supply-chain controls; trust in the producer is separate

threat: Change lands without independent review
note: no second human reviewer (Source L4): #14

threat: Source control management compromised (history rewrite, branch deletion)
note: no source provenance attestations yet: #14

threat: Build from unofficial ref or parameters
controls: R1 C14 C15 C16 ext:release-approved-source ext:release-provenance ext:reusable-build-workflow ext:release-verify-before-publish
note: release verify enforces approved source: strict vX.Y.Z tag pointing at the built commit, commit reachable from protected main; provenance pinned via --source-ref/--source-digest (R1 passes, C14-C16 reject off-main/bad-ref/retargeted). Assumes tag push = repo write access (single maintainer, #14)

threat: Build process tampered or non-hermetic
note: pinned toolchain; release requires two independent builds with identical sha256 (v0.1.0: 7fe80764...585f)

threat: Published artifact differs from built artifact
note: published assets are the verified build outputs plus their Sigstore bundles

threat: Distribution channel compromised
note: consumers detect replacement with gh attestation verify (also offline via the attached bundle; tampered binary rejected in test)

threat: Consumer selects the wrong package
note: consumer side; template is not published (publish = false)

threat: Consumer uses the artifact unsafely
note: consumer side

threat: Shipped code panics on unexpected input (denial of service)
note: S1e forbids (-F) the panic lints on non-test code, so #[allow] in the code is itself an error (C33); C26 plants indexing. Not covered: assert!, slice::split_at, Vec::remove, Index::index, code under #[cfg(not(clippy))] (round 3, A5): #45

threat: The gates judge a variant of the code that is not shipped (cfg(test)/debug_assertions/kani/fuzzing/clippy fork, or a runtime 'am I under cargo?' check)
controls: S1f S1g C36 C37 C38 C39 C40 C41 C42
note: S1f runs the test binaries built in RELEASE directly under env -i (C36 env fork, C39 debug_assertions fork); S1g rejects cfg/cfg!/cfg_attr on judging contexts in shipped source except #[cfg(test|kani)] on a mod item, and CARGO_*/RUST_TEST* literals (C37 cfg(test), C38 debug_assertions, C40 kani, C41 clippy, C42 a multi-line cfg expression; comments and string literals ignored). Residuals: S1g is a text scan (macros, concat!-built names, build.rs-set cfgs can hide a fork); unit tests in src/ still compile under cfg(test) - behaviour against a cfg(test) fork needs the spec in tests/: #45

threat: A change weakens the spec together with the code to hide a regression
note: Base-branch spec (tests + Kani harnesses, list read from base) runs on PR code; scripts taken from base; canaries SE1/SE2 break code AND weaken spec. Deliberate break needs owner label after last push. Residuals (not required yet, new behaviour has no base spec, spec independence O4): #37. Round 3: the worktree is read-only to the jailed build (SE3: a build.rs rewriting src/tests.rs), and every base spec file the base compiles must be compiled with the PR's code (SE4: an inline mod tests shadowing the file). Kani-mode shadowing still open: #45

threat: A claim is reported stronger than its evidence (bounded or model result read as any-input proof)
note: claims.tsv states scope code/model/bounded; verdict per axis PASS/FAIL/ABSTAIN from sealed gate results and kani-results.tsv; only scope=code may PASS the any-input axis; 7 verdict canaries. Not yet a required check: #37. scope=code is not taken on the claim's word: any-input PASS needs every evidence item to be a Kani proof or the no-panic lint gate (canary U; a bounded->code edit of claims.tsv gives ABSTAIN)

threat: A PASS rests on an unstated assumption, or on one no test ever violated (spec and code agree in the same error)
note: assumptions.tsv: every claim lists its assumptions; each is broken on purpose by a canary (gate expect=fail or Kani canary) that must have fired for its reason, else the claim FAILs; no list -> ABSTAIN; trusted:<reason> allowed but printed with every PASS. 5 ABG canaries in claims-check. Residual: spec independence itself (CA1.A4 trusted) needs a second blind spec (O4b): #37. At least one assumption per claim must be broken by a canary (all-trusted -> ABSTAIN, canary T). Breaker-assumption link is not semantic: #45

threat: Vulnerable or yanked dependency
note: cargo-deny advisories + cargo-audit; C9 proves the audit fires

threat: Disallowed license or unknown source
note: cargo-deny licenses/sources; C4 proves the license check fires

threat: Freshly published malicious version pulled in
note: 7-day cooldown; every cargo call uses --locked

threat: A gate reports PASS without performing its check (silent skip)
controls: C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 C9 C10 C11 C12 lean:CL20 lean:CL21
note: every Rust and Lean gate has a canary; witness inventory is sealed

threat: Toolchain drift between CI and local
note: exact Rust and Lean pins checked against the running tools

threat: Tests run code without checking it
note: coverage threshold + mutation testing

threat: Gate evidence forged or replaced
controls: E1 C17 C18 C19 lean:CL21 ext:fixture-evidence-checker ext:evidence-attestation ext:release-verify-evidence
note: green main runs sign sealed evidence (in-toto test-result v0.1, Sigstore, bound to commit); release refuses without a verified PASSED attestation. Witnessed on 3e27e9d (run 44148524796): PASSED, 74 passed / 0 failed; wrong commit digest and a 1-byte tamper both rejected. Release-side job first runs in CI at the next tag

threat: Proved model and shipped code diverge
controls: lean:L2 lean:X1 lean:X2 ext:kani-gate ext:kani-canaries lean:L4 lean:CL38 lean:CL39
note: Lean theorem <-> Rust test mapping only; Rust-level proof (Kani) pending: #20. Round 3: the axiom audit accepts only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (CL38: a user axiom proving 1 = 2 was accepted before); the built Lean sources must equal the PR's (L4, CL39: a file rewriting itself at elaboration)

threat: Malicious or unsafe workflow change
note: zizmor on every PR, CodeQL (actions) on push/PR

threat: AI agent PR carries injected instructions or edits the pipeline
controls: A1 A2 C20 C21 C22 C23 C24 C25 ext:workflow-approval ext:agent-pr-policy
note: agent/bot PRs touching the pipeline need the owner-approved-pipeline label from a human owner (revoked on every push); agent PRs need a clean Codex review on HEAD; policy runs from main. approval must postdate the latest push; Codex state trusted only from the exact integration (login + Bot). Residuals: (1) an agent using the owner's own token (Claude via gh) is indistinguishable from the owner - procedural rule only; (2) any same-repo workflow with statuses:write can post the same status context; live witness on #28: no label -> failure; owner label + clean Codex -> success; new push -> label auto-revoked by github-actions[bot] -> failure. agent-pr-policy is a REQUIRED check in the main ruleset since 2026-11-17 (repo admins may bypass via pull request only): #18

threat: Untested input space (parsers, adversarial inputs)
note: scripts/fuzz-gate.sh: every target in fuzz/fuzz-targets.tsv compares the real code with an independent reference; every target cargo-fuzz knows must be listed; canaries plant a bug in the REAL code and the REAL target must crash for its reason; corpus persists (restored each run, saved by main only); fuzz code jailed. Residuals: time-bounded search, not a required check (path-filtered PR runs + weekly), pilot targets: #19. Round 3: build and session are timed separately; a clean exit before 90% of the budget is FAIL (FC2: a target that prints 'Done' and calls exit_group). Writable fuzz paths may not be symlinks (C34)

threat: Code under test (build.rs, proc macros, tests, Lean elaboration) rewrites the evidence, scripts, config or runner command files of the job that judges it
controls: S0s S0f C28 C29 C30 C31 C32 C34 C35
note: ci-local, kani-gate, spec-epoch and fuzz-gate jail every code-executing cargo/elan/kani call in bubblewrap: filesystem read-only (dependency cache included) except a private TMPDIR, the target dir, its own work dir and explicit non-symlink paths (C34); environment cleared to toolchain variables and $HOME emptied (C35: a fake secret in env and $HOME is not readable); no network, IPC or PID namespace shared; empty /run and /tmp, other unix sockets masked (a read-only bind does not stop connect(): docker.sock was a full escape); Actions tokens and command-file paths unset. C28 write probe, C29 planted #[test] on results.tsv, C30 disarmed jail stops the next gate, C31 socket+network probe with a host decoy; network steps (fetch, metadata, deny, audit) run outside the jail but from an empty directory with explicit paths and precomputed metadata, so a checkout .cargo/config.toml (rustc-wrapper) is never read there - C32 plants such a wrapper and it may run only inside the jail; the kani, spec-epoch and fuzz jobs run the write and socket probes. Residuals (rust-toolchain.toml path= toolchains for the first unjailed rustc call, verdict inputs written by tests, shared kernel, verdicts computed in the same VM): #39 and #45
